payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier higher claim. The chemistry delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density and has a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its principal operating limitation is a 4 °C floor, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.
